topic: Re-measurement of the session-80 digest figures: Artificial Analysis latency, web_search latency, repo-measured S78/S80 numbers, Railway headers, Supabase Auth limits, Expo SDK 54 / Sentry defaults, RN Share, search-API retirements (checked 2026-10-22)

facts.claim: (1a) Artificial Analysis, Haiku 5.5 low: 7.8 s to the first answer token at 166 tok/s (10K-token input)
evidence: https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/claude-haiku-5-5-low/providers (read 2026-10-22): 6.61 s TTFAT, 171.3 tok/s, 9.52 s E2E for 500 tokens, 10,000-token input, Anthropic only
Latency figures are P50 over a rolling 72 h with no fixed date, so the digest's 7.83 s / 166 tok/s / 10.8 s was an earlier snapshot
facts.correction: Today it reads 6.61 s TTFAT, 171.3 tok/s and 9.52 s end to end. Cite it as a rolling 72 h median with the read date, not as a fixed number.

facts.claim: (1b) Artificial Analysis, Haiku 5.5 medium: 12.6 s to the first answer token
evidence: https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/claude-haiku-5-5-medium/providers (read 2026-10-22): 9.61 s TTFAT, 177.8 tok/s, 12.42 s E2E for 500 tokens, 10K input
A search-engine snippet of the same page still shows 12.63 s, so the digest copied an older rolling value
facts.correction: Today it reads 9.61 s TTFAT, and 12.42 s is the 500-token end-to-end time. The figure moves from window to window.

facts.claim: (1c) Artificial Analysis, Sonnet 5.5 high: 11.3 s TTFT and 16.4 s end to end for 500 tokens
evidence: https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/claude-sonnet-5-5-high/providers (read 2026-10-22): 'Claude Sonnet 5.5 (high with fallback)', 11.01 s TTFAT, 103.6 tok/s, 15.84 s E2E for 500 tokens, 10K input, Anthropic only
facts.correction: Today it reads 11.01 s TTFAT and 15.84 s end to end at 103.6 tok/s. The digest's 11.3 s, 16.4 s and about 98 tok/s came from an earlier 72 h window. Both readings are close.

facts.claim: (1d) Artificial Analysis publishes thinking-off (non-reasoning) variants of Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5
evidence: https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/claude-haiku-5-5-non-reasoning and .../claude-sonnet-5-5-non-reasoning both return HTTP 404 (2026-10-22)

Search (2026-10-22) shows only effort variants for 5.5 (Haiku low/medium/high/xhigh/max; Sonnet low/medium/high, 'Adaptive Reasoning ... Default Fallback'). Non-reasoning pages exist only for Sonnet 5, not 5.5
facts.correction: None is published. A thinking-off Haiku or Sonnet 5.5 latency has to be measured ourselves.

facts.claim: (1e) The Artificial Analysis figures reflect a 2-5K-token prompt
evidence: Every page fetched 2026-10-22 states a 10,000-input-token workload (the default since AA changed its benchmark workload to 10k)
facts.correction: They reflect a 10K-token input. No figure for a 2-5K prompt is published, so a lower TTFT for our smaller prompts is an inference, not a measurement.

facts.claim: (2) Anthropic publishes a per-search latency for the web_search tool
evidence: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool (read 2026-10-22): no timing figure. It only says 'There is a pause while the search runs' (streaming) and that long turns may return pause_turn
Same page: $10 per 1,000 searches; 'Simple factual queries typically use 1–3 searches'; Batches API throttles web search per org
facts.correction: No latency is published, so it must be measured. The digest's 'several seconds per search' is an inference. Its Brave/Exa/SerpAPI p50s are third-party benchmarks.

facts.claim: (3k) Supabase p50 381 ms per read
evidence: prod_evidence.json: 'GET /rest/v1/product_specs 30 and GET /rest/v1/product_reviews 30 extrapolated (about 3 sampled each), all in text_compare_get, 2026-10-14 03:50-04:26Z, p50 381 ms', status invalid_argument (4xx)
facts.correction: 381 ms is the p50 of FAILED (4xx) L2 cache reads: about 6 sampled spans in the window 2026-10-14 03:50-04:26Z. It is not a general per-read Supabase latency.

facts.claim: (4) Railway documents X-Real-IP and X-Forwarded-For and says whether it overwrites or appends client values
evidence: https://docs.railway.com/networking/public-networking/specs-and-limits (read 2026-10-22): documents X-Real-IP ('for identifying client's remote IP'), X-Forwarded-Proto (always https), X-Forwarded-Host, X-Railway-Edge, X-Railway-Request-Id. It does NOT mention X-Forwarded-For and states no overwrite/append rule
https://docs.railway.com/reference/edge-networking (read 2026-10-22): only says the edge 'terminates TLS, adds headers'

https://station.railway.com/questions/x-forwarded-for-behavior-edge-overwrit-e3663b39 and https://station.railway.com/questions/does-the-edge-strip-client-x-forwarded-f-613e5cb6 (search 2026-10-22): staff answers contradict each other (strip vs append); staff say the docs give no anti-spoofing guarantee
facts.correction: Only X-Real-IP is documented, and only by name. X-Forwarded-For handling is undocumented and the forum reports conflict. It could be settled by a written Railway answer or our own spoof test (send a fake X-Forwarded-For/X-Real-IP to a non-prod service and log what arrives).

facts.claim: (5) Supabase Auth limits: sign-ups 30 per 5 min per IP, /token 150 per 5 min per IP, built-in email 2 per hour per project, and Sb-Forwarded-For needs new secret API keys plus a dashboard toggle
evidence: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/rate-limits (read 2026-10-22): /signup,/recover,/resend,/magiclink,/otp,/user 30 per 5 min per IP (burst 30); /token 150 per 5 min per IP (burst 30; password, refresh, ID token, PKCE); built-in email '2 emails per hour' per project

Same page: Sb-Forwarded-For needs a secret API key ('Publishable API keys and legacy anon/service_role API keys are not supported') and 'must be explicitly enabled for new projects' under Authentication > Rate Limits > IP Address Forwarding, or via the Management API security_sb_forwarded_for_enabled
facts.correction: Precision: the 30/5 min bucket is shared by sign-up, recover, resend, magic link, OTP and /user. Password sign-in goes through /token (150/5 min). /verify is 30/5 min; anonymous sign-ins 30/h; MFA 15/min.

facts.claim: (6a) Expo SDK 54 tree shaking: default state and env gates in @expo/cli 54.0.x
evidence: C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-s79-b3client/SmartCompareApp/node_modules/@expo/cli/build/src/utils/env.js:193-197 (cli 54.0.24): EXPO_UNSTABLE_TREE_SHAKING and EXPO_UNSTABLE_METRO_OPTIMIZE_GRAPH both boolish default false

Same tree, build/src/start/server/metro/instantiateMetro.js:186-187 throws 'EXPO_UNSTABLE_TREE_SHAKING requires EXPO_UNSTABLE_METRO_OPTIMIZE_GRAPH'; middleware/metroOptions.js:63,69 apply them only in production and outside node

https://docs.expo.dev/guides/tree-shaking/ (read 2026-10-22): 'Enabled by default in SDK 54 and later' sits under the experimentalImportSupport step; the guide still asks for EXPO_UNSTABLE_TREE_SHAKING=1
facts.correction: Tree shaking is OFF by default. Only experimentalImportSupport is on by default, true in @expo/metro-config 54.0.15. Both env vars must be set, and the CLI throws when TREE_SHAKING is set without OPTIMIZE_GRAPH; the docs wrongly call that var optional. Caveat: verified on installed cli 54.0.24 in a sibling worktree. sc-s80-b2 has no node_modules and its lockfile pins @expo/cli 54.0.27 (package-lock.json:7028). The repo sets neither var and its metro.config.js is stock plus cacheVersion.

evidence: https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v54.0.0/config/app/ (read 2026-10-22): checkAutomatically 'ON_LOAD (default value)'; fallbackToCacheTimeout 'Defaults to 0' (range 0-300000 ms)
C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-s80-b2/SmartCompareApp/app.json:275-277: updates block sets only url, so the defaults apply (expo-updates 29.0.20 per package-lock.json:7497-7498)

facts.claim: (6c) getSentryExpoConfig accepts includeWebReplay and includeWebFeedback
evidence: C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-s79-b3client/SmartCompareApp/node_modules/@sentry/react-native/dist/js/tools/metroconfig.d.ts:16 (7.2.0): includeWebReplay?: boolean (default true; on ios/android the replay package resolves empty when undefined, metroconfig.js:125-128). No includeWebFeedback
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getsentry/sentry-react-native/main/CHANGELOG.md (read 2026-10-22): includeWebFeedback added in 8.10.0 (#6025)
C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-s80-b2/SmartCompareApp/metro.config.js: uses expo/metro-config getDefaultConfig, not getSentryExpoConfig; @sentry/react-native ~7.2.0 (package.json:22)
facts.correction: In the pinned 7.2.0 only includeWebReplay exists. includeWebFeedback needs @sentry/react-native 8.10.0 or later, which is a major bump and a native change, so it waits for 1.0.1. The repo does not use getSentryExpoConfig at all today.

facts.claim: (7a) React Native Share.share on iOS drops message when url is present
evidence: C:/Users/SynAckITPC/Documents/AI/sc-s79-b3client/SmartCompareApp/node_modules/react-native/React/CoreModules/RCTActionSheetManager.mm:225-251 (RN 0.81.5): adds BOTH message and URL to the UIActivityViewController items
https://reactnative.dev/docs/share (read 2026-10-22): no statement that message is dropped
facts.correction: RN passes both on iOS. Whether a given share target (an app extension) uses only the URL is that target's behaviour, which RN does not control and nobody here has measured. The opposite holds on Android: Libraries/Share/Share.js:107-112 forwards only title and message, so url is dropped there.

facts.claim: (7b) Android always reports sharedAction
evidence: https://reactnative.dev/docs/share (read 2026-10-22): 'In Android, returns a Promise which will always be resolved with action being Share.sharedAction'; dismissedAction is iOS-only
node_modules/react-native/Libraries/Share/Share.js:52 (0.81.5)

facts.claim: (8a) Google Programmable Search JSON API is closed to new customers and ends 2027-01-01
evidence: https://developers.google.com/custom-search/v1/overview (read 2026-10-22, page 'Last updated 2026-02-18'): 'closed to new customers'; existing customers 'have until January 1, 2027 to transition'; 100 free/day then $5 per 1,000 up to 10k/day; Vertex AI Search suggested for up to 50 domains

facts.claim: (8b) Bing Search APIs were retired 2025-08-11
evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/announcements/bing-search-api-retirement (ms.date 2025-05-15, read 2026-10-22): 'Bing Search APIs will be retired on August 11, 2025'; migrate to Grounding with Bing Search (Azure AI Agents)

facts.claim: (8c) Brave Search API image pricing: about $5 per 1,000 with images included and $5 free credit a month
evidence: https://brave.com/search/api/ (read 2026-10-22): Search plan '$5 per 1,000 requests', '$5 in free credits every month', 50 QPS, covers 'URLs, text, news, images, and more'; Answers $4 per 1,000 plus $5 per M tokens
facts.correction: No separate per-1,000 price for the Images endpoint is published. Image calls fall under the Search plan, which is an inference from the plan text. Older doc tiers ($3 Base / $5 Pro) and third-party resellers ($3) conflict, so confirm on the Brave dashboard.
